From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com

Subject: Follow-up: encryption controls, rotation and telemetry (post-demo)

Hi Anita — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Per our demo, quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the security workshop: 

Summary from demo:
- In transit: TLS 1.2/1.3 with mTLS option for Private deployments.
- At rest: AES-256 default; we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations and HSM-based wrapping.
- Telemetry/logging: token-level latency/cost traces available; audit logs for request metadata retained per account policy.

Questions for your security/ops team (answers will determine whether we propose Hosted w/Encryption/Private deployment or Dedicated + HSM):
1) Do you require customer-managed keys (CMKs) (yes/no)? If yes, do you prefer cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP Cloud KMS / Azure Key Vault) or an on-prem HSM?
2) Minimum key rotation cadence? Any enforced rotation via KMS or do you handle rotation externally?
3) Retention window for request/audit logs (event metadata vs payload) — any regulatory floor we should honor?
4) Is sampling of request bodies allowed for telemetry/regression debugging, or must bodies be redacted entirely?
5) Any required artifacts for procurement (SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration diagram, example logs)?

I attached the brief security Q we use for scoping (crestcap_security_q1.pdf) and a one-page keystore options matrix (redwood-keystore-options.xlsx).

Proposed next step: 45-minute ops workshop next week with your Sec+Infra to align on KMS/HSM path. Are you available Tue/Wed afternoon PST?

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
https://www.redwood.com

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and for the materials. I've looped in the security mailbox and added a couple answers inline below. See also the attached internal notes (we'll send a formal questionnaire separately).

Answers inline:
1) CMKs: yes — Crest prefers customer-managed keys. Primary path is AWS KMS (we run most workloads in AWS), but our security team may require HSM-backed key material for specific workloads (PCI/credit decisioning).
2) Rotation: policy is yearly rotation by default, but we rotate quarterly for high-sensitivity keys. Ideally we want Redwood to support rotation via KMS API (i.e., Redwood triggers rewrap or accepts rotated key versions from AWS KMS).
3) Retention: audit metadata (headers, timestamps, model id) — 7 years for certain regulated data; request payloads with PII must be retained no longer than 90 days unless explicitly consented.
4) Sampling: no sampling of PII-containing request bodies. We can allow sampled non-PII telemetry (token counts, latencies).
5) Artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, diagrams for KMS integration, and an example of redact/telemetry separation. We will accept artifacts via secure ShareFile or a signed SFTP.

We can do a workshop Wednesday 4/4 at 10:00 AM PST. Does that work on your side?

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Security Engineering | Crest Capital
anita.rao@crestcap.com

[Attachment: crestcap_internal_notes.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Marissa — quick answers from infra/serving runtime perspective:
- AWS KMS BYOK: supported today for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we support envelope encryption with customer-provided KMS keys in select accounts (we'll confirm current rollout status). We can accept rotated key versions; the recommended pattern is to rely on AWS KMS key aliases and let KMS handle rotation while Redwood uses the alias. That avoids re-encrypt cycles at Redwood if they keep the same alias.
- HSM-backed path: we have an HSM-wrapping option for Dedicated; for Private we can plug into on-prem HSMs during deployment. For Hosted, HSM-backed BYOK is available via Cloud HSM integrations but requires additional procurement/contract terms.
- Rotation: we can support a rotation workflow where Redwood picks up new key versions via KMS API and rewraps existing data lazily; for real-time session keys there is no service interruption. Quarterly rotation is feasible but recommend a staged rollout to avoid mass rewrap overhead.
- Retention: metadata retention is configurable by account; we'll need to implement a hard retention policy for PII payloads at 90d (we have deletion APIs but may need a policy enforcement flag to be added to the account config).

I'll join the 4/4 workshop and bring a short slide with architecture paths.

-Ben
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
